Job Description
The Role:
We're a bold, creative crew of designers and strategists embedded in GM Industrial Design, where innovation meets imagination. We specialize in visual storytelling powered by cutting-edge graphics, AI, and design thinking—turning brand values and market insights into visuals that move people.
The Team:
GM’s Industrial Design organization brings together a global community of designers, makers, and creative technologists who shape the physical and digital character of GM vehicles and customer experiences. Working across disciplines and studios, teams move ideas from research and 2D concepts through digital and physical development into compelling experiences for GM’s portfolio of brands. As an intern, you will learn in a collaborative, feedback-driven environment while partnering with designers, engineers, suppliers, and fabrication experts to explore how form, color, material, finish, graphics, and technology come together.
We are hiring interns in Industrial Design across two focus areas for Summer 2027:
Brand ID + Product Design Intern:
This role will support the development of distinctive vehicle accessories and graphics by turning creative 2D concepts into compelling 3D applications. Projects may include accessory badges and emblems, decals and wrap graphics, wheel and exterior details, branded charging/cargo/utility accessories, and explorations of material, finish, scale, and placement. The intern will also create physical or digital prototypes to support design reviews and bring ideas to life on the vehicle.
Colors, Materials, Finish (CMF) Intern:
This role will support the design of future vehicles through research and development in color, materials, and finish. Projects may include exploring CMF trends, developing color and material palettes, researching sustainable and innovative materials, and defining textures, gloss levels, patterns, and surface treatments for interior and exterior applications. The intern may also create physical and digital samples, support prototype development, collaborate with suppliers, and prepare visual presentations for design reviews.
What You’ll Do:
Explore ideas that enhance the design, identity, and customer experience of future vehicles.
Research trends, materials, technologies, and user perspectives to inform design concepts.
Develop and communicate concepts through sketches, visual studies, samples, models, and prototypes.
Translate creative ideas into thoughtful applications across vehicle surfaces, accessories, and experiences.
Collaborate with designers, engineers, suppliers, and other partners to refine and realize concepts.
Present work, receive feedback, and iterate designs throughout the development process.
Please note, you must submit a portfolio to be considered for this position – see instructions below.
Required Qualifications:
• Pursuit of a bachelor's or BFA degree in Industrial Design, Product Design, Interior Design, Graphic Design, CMF, or related creative discipline.
• Must be graduating between December 2027 and May 2029.
• Able to work full-time, 40 hours per week during the summer months.
Preferred Qualification
• Knowledge of AI programs such as Vizcom and Midjourney.
• Knowledge of VRED, Adobe Suite (Illustrator, Photoshop), Alias, Blender
• A sharp eye for what's next, bringing trend-savvy taste, techniques, and cultural awareness to inspire the studio and maintain a creative edge.
• Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.
• Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work both in teams and independently.
• Excellent communication skills.
• Dependability.
• Strong organizational and project-planning skills.

Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.
At Micron, we are transforming how the world uses information to enrich life. The High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) Design team develops industry-leading memory solutions that power Artificial Intelligence (AI), high-performance computing, graphics, and data center applications. Our team collaborates across Design, Verification, Physical Design, Product Engineering, and CAD organizations to deliver next-generation memory technologies.
As an HBM Design Engineer Intern, you will work alongside experienced engineers on the design, development, and validation of advanced HBM products. This internship provides hands-on experience with semiconductor design methodologies, industry-standard EDA tools, and AI-assisted engineering workflows while contributing to real-world memory design projects in a collaborative global environment.
Responsibilities
Assist with HBM memory and logic design activities, including RTL development, circuit implementation, simulation, verification, and functional analysis.
Develop and use scripting, automation, and AI-assisted workflows to improve design productivity, debug efficiency, and design-flow quality.
Perform timing, power, and functional analysis of HBM subsystems and support design reviews, technical investigations, and root-cause analysis using AI-enabled engineering techniques where appropriate.
Collaborate with Design Verification, Physical Design, CAD, and Product Engineering teams to support project execution and product development.
Document technical work, experimental results, build methodologies, and AI-assisted insights to support collaboration and ongoing improvement.
Minimum Qualifications
Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field.
Completed coursework in Digital Logic Design, CMOS Circuits, Computer Architecture, VLSI Design, Semiconductor Devices, or equivalent subjects.
Demonstrated understanding of combinational and sequential logic design concepts and familiarity with Verilog, SystemVerilog, or VHDL.
Programming experience in Python, Perl, Tcl, C/C++, or similar languages.
Strong analytical, debugging, problem-solving, communication, and teamwork skills.
Preferred Qualifications
Knowledge of memory architectures such as DRAM, SRAM, DDR, LPDDR, or HBM.
Experience with RTL design, simulation, synthesis, timing analysis, or verification methodologies through coursework, research, or internships.
Familiarity with Linux/Unix environments, scripting, and semiconductor EDA tools such as VCS, Xcelium, Questa, PrimeTime, Innovus, or Virtuoso.
Understanding of functional coverage, design verification concepts, and semiconductor development flows.
Previous academic, research, or internship experience involving VLSI, ASIC, FPGA, memory design, or the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to enhance engineering productivity and analysis.
As a world leader in the semiconductor industry, Micron is dedicated to your personal wellbeing and professional growth. Micron benefits are designed to help you stay well, provide peace of mind and help you prepare for the future. We offer a choice of medical, dental and vision plans in all locations enabling team members to select the plans that best meet their family healthcare needs and budget. Micron also provides benefit programs that help protect your income if you are unable to work due to illness or injury, and paid family leave. Additionally, Micron benefits include a robust paid time-off program and paid holidays. For additional information regarding the Benefit programs available, please see the Benefits Guide posted on micron.com/careers/benefits.

The Role
This is a summer internship opportunity in Norwood, MA from June 7, 2027 – August 20, 2026. Applicants must be available for the entire duration of the internship. Start date will be June 7, 2027.
Moderna’s Applied Technologies team develops and deploys innovative automation, robotics, and digital solutions that enable faster, more reliable, and more scalable scientific and technical workflows.
As an Applied Technologies Intern, you will work alongside engineers and scientists to support the design, development, testing, and implementation of automation solutions used across Technical Development. You will have the opportunity to gain hands-on experience with laboratory automation, robotics, software, data, and systems engineering while contributing to a defined technical project with real-world impact.
This role is designed for a curious, hands-on learner who enjoys solving technical problems, working across disciplines, and translating ideas into practical solutions.
Here’s What You’ll Do
Contribute to a defined automation, robotics, or systems engineering project under the guidance of an AT engineer or scientist.
Support the development, configuration, and testing of laboratory automation systems, robotic platforms, instruments, or related software.
Assist with experimental execution, system characterization, troubleshooting, and collection of performance data.
Analyze test or experimental data and summarize findings to support engineering decisions.
Develop or modify scripts, workflows, automation methods, or simple software tools where appropriate.
Support preparation of test plans, technical documentation, diagrams, work instructions, and project summaries.
Participate in prototype development and evaluate potential improvements to system reliability, throughput, usability, or scalability.
Work collaboratively with scientists, engineers, automation specialists, and other Technical Development partners to understand user needs and technical requirements.
Apply good engineering and documentation practices, including appropriate use of version control and structured testing.
Present project progress, technical findings, and recommendations to the Applied Technologies team at the conclusion of the internship.
Learn about the application of automation, robotics, systems engineering, and digital technologies within biotechnology development.
Bring curiosity, initiative, and a willingness to learn as part of a team that values being Bold, Relentless, Curious, and Collaborative.
Here’s What You’ll Need (Basic Qualifications)
Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or graduate degree in an engineering, computer science, bioengineering, robotics, automation, life sciences, or related technical discipline.
Completion of relevant coursework or project experience involving one or more of the following:
programming or scripting;
robotics or mechatronics;
laboratory automation;
electrical or mechanical systems;
systems engineering;
data analysis;
biological or laboratory sciences.
Demonstrated interest in applying engineering or digital technologies to scientific problems.
Ability to work effectively in a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment.
Strong problem-solving, organizational, and communication skills.
Ability to document work clearly and communicate technical results.
Here’s What You’ll Bring to the Table (Preferred Qualifications)
GPA of 3.5 on a 4 scale or equivalent.
Hands-on academic, research, internship, maker-space, or personal project experience with automation or robotics.
Programming experience in Python, C#, JavaScript, MATLAB, or a similar language.
Experience working with laboratory instruments, liquid handlers, robotic systems, sensors, microcontrollers, or electromechanical systems.
Familiarity with CAD, Git/version control, data visualization, or engineering analysis tools.
Experience designing and executing experiments or structured technical tests.
Exposure to biological laboratory workflows or biotechnology/pharmaceutical development.
Interest in emerging technologies such as machine learning, computer vision, autonomous systems, or advanced robotics.

Accountants that demonstrate exceptional proficiency are eligible for opportunities within other areas of the Company, where the analytical skills developed while in the Controller's Organization are highly valued. Accountants often transfer to operational components of the business such as: Refining, Commercial, Logistics & Storage, Pipeline and Gathering & Processing. An exciting career awaits you
At MPC, we’re committed to being a great place to work – one that welcomes new ideas, encourages diverse perspectives, develops our people, and fosters a collaborative team environment.
Responsibilities:
As a Chemical Engineer at a Marathon refinery, you can expect to become familiar with process equipment fundamentals and best practices, build critical thinking skills, and gain an understanding of how all engineering disciplines work together as a cohesive team. You will also gain knowledge of various aspects of a refinery by working with a team of professionals who run a specific portion of the refining process. Most often, Chemical Engineers will have an opportunity to work on more than one area of the refinery, leading to a broad understanding of how the plant operates. Finally, you will have the opportunity to expand your written and verbal presentation skills in a professional work environment.
Most Chemical Engineering co-ops and interns enter into the following positions:
Process / Technical Service Engineers may work on a variety of projects in the Technical Services Department together with your mentor that put your classroom experience as a Chemical Engineer into practice. The vast majority of our Chemical Engineering interns/co-ops work in this area. The experience will expand your understanding of the refining environment and technical aspects of the refinery. Past projects/duties include: develop and lead test runs to optimize refinery operations; perform process engineering calculations concerning the various process technology (or equipment) in the refinery; monitor and make recommendations in regards to catalyst and adsorbents; complete projects and provide recommendations for improvements to the refinery process and equipment.
Operations Research Engineers may help develop planning, blending, scheduling, and process models for refinery engineers. The models are used to optimize crude oil purchasing, refinery production, blending and finished product scheduling, and optimization of refinery production. Typical college co-op assignments include: validation of production data and mass balancing, process modeling, and development of graphical interfaces of refinery process units.
Environmental Engineers work on projects that involve the compliance of the entire refinery, and you will be exposed to the majority of process units in the refinery. Job Summary
What You’ll Do
1. Assist in the design and integration of control systems and vehicle electronics using foundational electrical engineering principles.
2. Support the creation and maintenance of electrical schematics using Computer-Aided Design (CAD) tools such as Zuken E3 or AutoCAD.
3. Help troubleshoot Controller Area Network (CAN) systems including tools like CANalyzer or Vector CANoe and perform basic diagnostics using multimeters and oscilloscopes.
4. Participate in testing and validation activities using data acquisition and analysis tools such as Dewesoft, MATLAB, or nCode.
5. Contribute to documentation and design tracking using Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) systems such as Dassault Systems 3DX, including exposure to Engineering Change Notification (ECN) processes.
6. Learn about and support the application of functional safety standards such as ISO 26262 or IEC 61508 in system design and testing.
What We’re Looking For
- Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Mechanical, Industrial, Agricultural Engineering, or relative equivalent discipline.
- Foundational understanding of electrical engineering principles, especially in control systems and vehicle electronics.
- Exposure to CAD tools (e.g., Zuken E3, AutoCAD), CAN protocols (e.g., SAE J1939), and data acquisition tools (e.g., MATLAB, Dewesoft).
- Interest in learning about functional safety and engineering change processes.
- Willingness to perform hands-on testing and troubleshooting in lab or field environments.
- Strong communication and collaboration skills with a growth mindset.
Travel
- Occasional travel is expected of this position.
Work Location
ONSITE: A team member’s day-to-day work is best done on a Vermeer campus. If work content can be occasionally completed at an offsite location, discuss potential arrangements with your manager.
